subject.title: Feature: Dynamic header templating for custom LLM providers (enables Fireworks.ai prompt caching)

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic runtime placeholder contract for provider headers, or keep session-aware provider headers limited to typed/provider-specific features?
rationale: Current main still has a source-level gap, but the requested config syntax can expose runtime identifiers to third-party providers and overlaps with open Fireworks, ZAI, ChatGPT Responses, schema, run-context, extra_body, and per-agent/per-cron header work.

options.title: Approve narrow explicit placeholders
options.body: Support only approved values such as {{session.key}}, {{agent.id}}, and {{run.id}} in configured provider request headers with docs and tests preserving static and SecretRef behavior.

options.title: Prefer typed/provider-specific mapping
options.body: Use provider-specific affinity flags or explicit run-context header mapping instead of arbitrary string templating in header values.

options.title: Defer for privacy design
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers define which runtime identifiers may be sent to external providers and how users opt in.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow explicit placeholders
recommendation.body: Support only approved values such as {{session.key}}, {{agent.id}}, and {{run.id}} in configured provider request headers with docs and tests preserving static and SecretRef behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman is the live assignee and best available owner for this product/security boundary decision.
